- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (0.17+), and correct downward bias in the 10-15 day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.22) or when recent prices are falling — model tends to lag mean reversion.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; if sentiment is volatile, reduce forecast amplitude.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to over-forecast; apply a 5-10% downward adjustment to the 30d forecast.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, reduce forecast slope for next 5 days — especially if sentiment was neutral or positive.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is below 70.00 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2-5% to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22) followed by recovery, model often overshoots — apply a “soft cap” to forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment turns neutral.
